title: Projection-normalized comparison of the integral completed coefficient presentations
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $A=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and any scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme]. Let $A^\uparrow$ denote the same ring raised to the small site's coefficient universe, with $d:A^\uparrow\xrightarrow{\sim}A$ the ring equivalence $x\mapsto x.\mathrm{down}$. Put $I=(\varpi.\mathrm{up})$, $P_n=A^\uparrow/I^n$ and $Q_n=(A/(\varpi^n))^\uparrow$ for $n\ge1$. On $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], use the normalized finite coefficient presentations of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and the inverse-limit completed integral coefficient sheaf of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. There are unique ring isomorphisms
$$e_n:P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_n,\qquad e_n([x])=[x.\mathrm{down}].\mathrm{up},$$
and they commute with every quotient transition. Write $(P_n)_T$ for the finite coefficient ring sheaf of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], the sheafification of $U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),P_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], and $(Q_n)_T$ for the constant ring sheaf of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], the sheafification of the constant presheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. The presheaf map sending an element of $P_n$ to the corresponding constant function induces, after sheafification, an isomorphism of ring sheaves $\kappa_n:\underline{P_n}\xrightarrow{\sim}(P_n)_T$, compatible with the quotient transitions. Put $\bar e_n=\underline{e_n}\circ\kappa_n^{-1}:(P_n)_T\xrightarrow{\sim}(Q_n)_T$. Let $B_T^{\mathrm{pbc}}=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_T$ and $B_T^{\mathrm{det}}=\varprojlim_n(Q_n)_T$, with projections $\pi_n^{\mathrm{pbc}}$ and $\pi_n^{\mathrm{det}}$. There is a unique ring-sheaf isomorphism $e_T:B_T^{\mathrm{pbc}}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_T^{\mathrm{det}}$ satisfying $\pi_n^{\mathrm{det}}e_T=\bar e_n\pi_n^{\mathrm{pbc}}$ for every $n\ge1$. Restriction along $e_T$ and its inverse are exact inverse equivalences on module sheaves [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Their unbounded derived equivalences [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] preserve cohomology bounds and identify derived finite reductions, their adjunction-unit maps, quotient transitions [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], and the associated product Roos diagrams $K\to\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nK_n$ of [def-weil-derived-complete] and [def-weil-derived-limit]. No constructibility or derived-completeness membership assertion is included.

proof.text: Build the natural transformation of completed projections by the inverse-limit equations, initially on successor arrows. The finite-level natural isomorphism induces an isomorphism of inverse limits. The commutative-to-ring forgetful functor preserves these limits and is fully faithful; transport the limit comparison back through it. Limit projections give the normalization and its uniqueness.

proof.text: Construct restriction along the identity sectionwise using restrictScalarsIdApp. Compose the normalized pbcRestrictComp comparisons for e and its inverse with these identity comparisons. This gives inverse scalar equivalences, hence exactness. Derive the inverse natural isomorphisms using the exact-functor compositor and identity comparison. The derived homology comparison preserves bounds; faithful exact restriction reflects vanishing and hence reflects every bound.

proof.text: For each projection square form r from the two pbcRestrictComp comparisons; both its maps are identity on underlying sections. Given adjunctions L ⊣ U and Lprime ⊣ Uprime and equivalences F and G with r:G U ≅ Uprime F, define alpha at X as the adjunct of F(unitprime X) followed by r inverse. Naturality follows from the two adjunction bijections. Precomposition with alpha is the composite of those bijections and the fully faithful equivalence bijections, so it is bijective for every target; thus alpha is invertible by Yoneda. Its defining adjunct equation is precisely the required unit compatibility.

proof.text: For an arbitrary quotient arrow form the restriction square s from the finite-level naturality equation. The ordinary composition coherence follows by evaluating its section maps, all identities. Apply the proved exact-derived-square composition theorem to descend this coherence. The generic adjunction calculation then identifies the two reduction transitions: applying the upper adjunction bijection reduces the equation to the unit identities and restriction coherence. This works for all a ≤ b without induction or a flatness assumption.

proof.text: Apply pro-etale countable-products exactness to each completed ring. Its product-of-epimorphisms clause makes the countable limit functor preserve epimorphisms; with left exactness this gives CountableAB4Star. The derived-product existence theorem supplies products of both reduction families.

proof.text: An equivalence preserves products. Compose its canonical product comparison with the product of the inverse level isomorphisms. Each projection is F(pr_n) followed by beta_n inverse. The unit equation identifies the first Roos arrow after all projections. The transition equation identifies the product shifts after all projections. Additivity then identifies their differences from the identity, which are the actual 1-s maps.

tool_uses.why: The coefficient valuation ring is a DVR with finite residue field; generic coefficient arithmetic, not a replacement for proper base change.
Finiteness of each positive quotient is needed for the finite-constant-sections theorem; the unit contains no separate coefficient-arithmetic result.
Its normalized section isomorphisms identify constant and continuous-function finite coefficient sheaves on arbitrary schemes.
Exact scalar equivalence and preservation of flat and K-flat complexes for an arbitrary ring-sheaf isomorphism.
Termwise descent of exact scalar equivalences to unbounded derived categories.
Existence of flat-term K-flat resolutions for the arbitrary unbounded module complex.
Computation and canonical resolution independence of finite derived reductions, for possibly nonflat quotient maps.
The genuine unbounded scalar adjunction has the unit x mapped to x tensor 1 on a flat-term K-flat model.
Exact countable products for module sheaves over either completed ring on an arbitrary small pro-etale site.

Source: Bhatt-Scholze section 6.5 and Lemma 4.2.12 (F_T, discrete T constant), read in the PDF. All 11 steps checked against the statements they cite. Step 1: the up/down ring iso carries I^n onto (varpi^n). Step 2: integers-dvr cl. 2-4 plus valued-dvr-finite-quotients cl. 2; nonarchimedean comes from the coefficient definition. Step 3: finite-constant-sections theta holds for any V; continuous maps to a discrete space factor through pi0 with the quotient topology, so the Cont(pi0) presheaf is already the sheaf underline(P_n) and kappa_n is the specified map; the qcqs clause of 4.2.12 is avoided. Step 4: sectionwise ring limits. Steps 5-6: ring-iso transport gives an exact equivalence; exact-functor-derived gives the derived equivalence and preserves bounds. Step 7: I checked the alpha_n balancing myself via pi^S_n e = b_n pi^R_n; resolution independence is derived-change-of-rings (2). Step 8: the adjunction unit is x->x tensor 1 on flat-term K-flat models with no flatness of phi, and the Res composition is correct; this gives c_n exactly. Step 9: transition squares and cocycle at chain level. Step 10: products-exact holds for any ring sheaf; derived-limit clause 2 only. Step 11: the equivalence preserves products, and the components of c and of 1-s agree; no triangle or completeness is claimed. Edge cases checked: T empty, M=0, unbounded M, non-qc or disconnected U, n=1. No duplicate found: def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, completed-constant-sheaf-reduction, proetale-constant-ring-map and the cbc/pur Cont-functoriality nodes are not this comparison. No changes.
